metadata.note: The Wilkes-Barre and Eastern Railroad (chartered 1892, a wholly owned NYS&W subsidiary) was a 64.5-mile single-track coal road from Wilkes-Barre (a terminal in Kingston) east via Plains, Suscon, the Panther Creek Viaduct, the Lehigh River, Pocono Lake and Pocono Summit, down Pocono Creek through Tannersville and Bartonsville to Stroudsburg, where it met the NYS&W's own main line. The NYS&W leased it from late 1893 and ran every train on it, so both features carry the NYS&W's company and colour (Rule 4: no ownership split; the Erie's stock control of the NYS&W 1898-1940 did not change the operator). Through passenger trains to Jersey City began 4 Jun 1894; from 1897 (or 1905) a single daily mixed train ran Plains - Stroudsburg until 15 May 1935. Freight lasted to March 1939 and the line was abandoned; the river bridge at Plains went to the Wilkes-Barre Connecting Railroad in 1940.

not_yet_sourced: End of through Jersey City trains: 1897 (Wikipedia, citing Mohowski 2003 p.44) vs 1905 (Diamond 2011, citing Fredericks 1986). Drawn with 1897 as the era boundary; Fredericks' WB&E book (Railroadians of America, 1986) would settle it.

Kingston - Plains terminal leg (nysw-wbe-kingston-plains): LOW CONFIDENCE. No source cleanly ties the 4 Jun 1894 opening to the Kingston station, and the 1894 Wilkes-Barre Times station list (via mrlocalhistory) names Ashley, Georgetown and Laurel Run, south of the city, not on the Plains - Kingston route. If that is not resolved in the station's favour this feature should be removed. Its end is withheld at 1897; the true end lies between 1897 and 1908.
No timetable has been seen for any year; both headways and the speed are estimates from narrative sources.
Whether the 1897-1935 mixed train always reached Stroudsburg station or (as in 1923) terminated at Shops, 0.8 mi short.
Positions of the Plains, Shops and NYS&W Stroudsburg stations and of the Kingston station were not located; see geometry_quality.

properties.geometry_quality: Plains - Stroudsburg: drawn 63.0 mi against a documented 61.5 mi (Fowler: Plains MP 3.0, Stroudsburg MP 64.5; the 1939 abandonment 'about 54 miles' Suscon - Stroudsburg vs Fowler 53.5). Router figures (63.3 mi before simplification): 50.1 mi on OSM ways tagged for the WB&E, 1.0 mi on untagged abandoned grade at Stroudsburg, 0.1 mi of Susquehanna Connecting track at the Suscon junction, 0.3 mi of short connectors, and 11.7 mi APPROXIMATE (hand-drawn Wikimedia Commons trace, not OSM) in five legs (lengths measured between the adjoining OSM ways, so they sum to about 12.6 mi): 0.4 mi east of Plains (between OSM ways 1328037005 and 138488969); 2.3 mi Yatesville - Suscon; 1.9 mi from north of Pocono Lake to Pocono Lake; 0.7 mi at Pocono Pines; and 7.3 mi from east of Tannersville through Bartonsville and Shops into Stroudsburg - the whole of the eastern end is a hand trace. No ruled straight-line legs. The Stroudsburg end is placed where the WB&E grade runs into the NYS&W's own line east of town (the east end of OSM way 777613320), beside the end of nysw-jerseycity-stroudsburg; the NYS&W Stroudsburg passenger station (Fowler MP 64.5) and Shops (MP 63.7, the 1923 terminus) were not individually located. The Plains end is placed 3.0 mi from the Kingston station along the plains-kingston feature (Fowler's MP 3.0), 0.3 km from Nominatim's Plains village node; the Plains station site itself was not located. ERA CAVEAT: drawn on the grade as OSM and the Commons trace show it, i.e. as abandoned in 1939; no realignment between 1894 and 1935 is known, but none was checked for.

segments.note: Wilkes-Barre and Eastern Railroad, leased to and operated by the New York, Susquehanna and Western from late 1893 (WB&E cars, locomotives and stations were lettered NYS&W). Through passenger service Jersey City - Wilkes-Barre began 4 Jun 1894 (Wikipedia, citing Mohowski 2003 p.44; first train left at 7:05 a.m. per the Wilkes-Barre Times quoted by mrlocalhistory), running over WB&E rails to Stroudsburg and NYS&W rails east of it: two trains each way daily (Wilkes-Barre Times 1894; one coach, one mail/smoker combine, one express car). END YEAR CONFLICTS: Wikipedia/Mohowski p.44 say the through trains were discontinued in 1897 'with mixed trains taking over local passenger business'; the Diamond (Erie Lackawanna Historical Society, 2011) says two daily trains each way ran Kingston - Jersey City 'until 1905'. 1897, the shorter figure, is used as the era boundary; it changes only the note and headway, not the drawn span. Headway c.720 min is an estimate from '2 trains each way daily', not counted from a timetable.
sources: Segment-level: start 4 Jun 1894 from Wikipedia (Mohowski 2003 p.44) and the Wilkes-Barre Times 1894 via mrlocalhistory; 2/day from the Wilkes-Barre Times via mrlocalhistory; 1897 end of through trains from Wikipedia (Mohowski p.44), conflicting with Diamond's 1905 (recorded, not resolved). No timetable seen.

segments.note: One daily mixed train each way Plains - Stroudsburg after the through trains ended (1897 per Mohowski; 1905 per Diamond). Confirmed mid-life by the 1914 Pennsylvania PSC decision W.A. Edgar v. NYS&W (complaint about the mixed train's slow, irregular schedule; the NYS&W agreed to cut half an hour each way, via Diamond) and by the 1923 Official Guide, in which the service ran Plains - Shops (Fowler, Plains and Shops tagged b = 1923G; Shops is 0.8 mi short of Stroudsburg station). The Erie's stock control of the NYS&W (1898-1940) did not change who ran the trains. Mixed-train operation, and with it all passenger service, ended 15 May 1935 (Wikipedia citing Mohowski 2003 p.44; Scranton Times quoted by mrlocalhistory; Diamond). Freight continued up to 3-4 times a week until abandonment in March 1939 - context only, not drawn (Rule 1). Locally the 'Turkey Line'. Headway c.1440 min is an estimate from 'one daily mixed train', not counted from a timetable.
sources: Segment-level: 1914 PSC case (W.A. Edgar v. NYS&W) via Diamond; 1923 Official Guide via Fowler section 249 (b = 1923G at Plains and Shops); end 15 May 1935 from Wikipedia (Mohowski 2003 p.44), Scranton Times via mrlocalhistory, and Diamond. Start year is the 1897 era boundary from Mohowski (1905 per Diamond). No timetable seen; headway not sourced.

properties.geometry_quality: Kingston (WB&E station, foot of Market Street bridge) - Plains: drawn 2.84 mi against Fowler's 3.0 mi (Wilkes-Barre (WBE) MP 0.0 - Plains MP 3.0). The Plains end was set at the point 3.0 mi along an earlier draft of this line; the Kingston station pin was then moved about 280 m east to the west end of the Market Street bridge (Nesbitt Park), shortening the line to 2.84 mi. Traced on OSM 2.25 mi. STRAIGHT-LINE LEGS: 0.48 mi from the hand-pinned Kingston station north up the west bank to the west end of the river bridge - the alignment of the WB&E's west-bank approach (and of the trestle removed in 1908) is not mapped anywhere and the station position itself is approximate; and 0.12 mi joining OSM ways 1134537802 and 1328037005 east of the river at Plains. About 0.6 mi straight in all. ERA CAVEAT: the river crossing is drawn on the present Sunbury Line bridge; whether that is the WB&E's 1890s bridge or a later replacement on the same site is not established.

segments.note: LOW CONFIDENCE. The WB&E's Wilkes-Barre terminal, a passenger station and freight house on the west bank in Kingston at the foot of the Market Street bridge (Fowler MP 0.0 'Wilkes-Barre (WBE)'; west2k), reached from Plains over the WB&E's own Susquehanna River bridge. The Diamond makes Kingston the terminal of the two daily Jersey City trains; the line opened for passengers on 4 Jun 1894 from 'its new station' in Wilkes-Barre, but no source cleanly ties that opening to this station, and the 1894 Wilkes-Barre Times station list quoted by mrlocalhistory (Wilkes-Barre, Ashley, Georgetown, Laurel Run ...) describes a route south of the city instead - unresolved. Drawn only to 1897, the earliest end any source permits (Mohowski's end of through service); the actual end lies between 1897 and 1908 (Diamond: trains to Kingston 'until 1905'; Fowler: a North Bridge St station 'used when bridge became unsafe in 1905?'; the trestle linking the station to the bridge was removed in 1908). Do not extend without evidence. The building later housed the Pennsylvania State School of Aero Mechanics (1918-26). Headway is an estimate from the 2/day through trains.
sources: Segment-level: LOW CONFIDENCE. Kingston as terminal of the through trains from Diamond (citing Fredericks 1986 / Mohowski); station site from Fowler section 249 and west2k; 1894 opening from Wikipedia (Mohowski p.44) and mrlocalhistory, not tied to this station; 1897 end is Mohowski's end of through service, used as the earliest permissible end. No timetable seen; headway not sourced.
